stories.headline: US-Iran conflict widens further: Iran claims destroying F-35s in a Kuwait base strike (unconfirmed by CENTCOM)
stories.verification: Confirmed-primary (Iran made the claim, via its own state media); Disputed/Unverified (the claim's substance, no US confirmation)
stories.one_line: Iran's army claims a drone strike destroyed 3 F-35s and damaged 3 more, killing personnel, at Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base, Kuwait, in retaliation for Wednesday's Qeshm Island strike. CENTCOM has not confirmed; a CNN headline explicitly frames it as "Iran claims attack...but US reports no fresh strikes." Forecast 2026-07-31-am-1 logged on non-confirmation within 48h. Saudi Arabia says 14 countries back its new Maritime Defense Alliance proposal.
stories.score_note: Conflict footprint keeps broadening on claims alone; highest-priority active thread, now hinging on independent confirmation.
sources: IRIB/Iranian Army Public Relations (state media, flagged)

stories.headline: Mega-cap earnings week closes out: Amazon posts first $200B+ quarter (AWS +37%), Apple beats too; Thursday's MSFT/META split still the week's defining split
stories.one_line: Amazon Q2: $200.6B net sales (+20% YoY, first time over $200B), AWS $42.2B (+37% YoY, 18-quarter high), operating income +43% to $27.5B; premarket +12%. Apple fiscal Q3: $109.4B revenue (+16% YoY, "strongest June quarter ever"), EPS $2.02 vs $1.88 est. Both beat after Thursday's close, following MSFT's historic +15.56% Wednesday-earnings rally and META's continuing -8.00% decline. Forecast 2026-07-30-pm-1 (either moves >5%) trending toward realized on Amazon's premarket move alone; formal resolution awaits today's close.
stories.score_note: Completes the week's five-mega-cap earnings arc; today's cash session is the real test of durability.

stories.headline: Russia launches a major missile/drone barrage on Ukraine overnight; a suspected Russian cruise missile crashes inside NATO member Poland
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (core event); Disputed (precise Ukraine casualty count, 8 vs 13 dead)
stories.one_line: Ukraine's FM Sybiha specifically identified the object that crashed in Poland as a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile. Polish PM Tusk convened an emergency meeting; multiple outlets report no current plans to invoke NATO Article 4, narrowing but not resolving forecast 2026-07-30-pm-3 (horizon 2026-08-02). Ukraine-wide casualty count from the same barrage remains disputed (8 vs 13).
stories.score_note: Direct NATO-territory security event; forecast tracking whether Article 4 is invoked.

stories.headline: Q2 2026 GDP prints 1.5%, a miss, as PCE inflation holds near 3.7%
stories.one_line: BEA's advance estimate: +1.5% annualized, down from Q1's +2.1%, missing most-cited consensus figures (1.8-2.3% range across providers). PCE inflation +3.7% YoY (down from 4.1% May). Forecast 2026-07-27-am-2 (1.0-2.5% range) resolves CORRECT; forecast 2026-07-30-am-2 (below-range print) resolves WRONG. GDPNow's final 1.5% nowcast matched the actual print almost exactly.
stories.score_note: Resolved; first hard data point after Wednesday's FOMC surprise, complicates rather than clarifies the policy outlook given weak growth alongside above-target inflation.

stories.headline: US chip stocks stage a sharp rebound, breaking a four-session losing streak
stories.one_line: Micron +18.4%, AMD +13.1%, Marvell +12.1% (this run's own data); wire coverage corroborates similar moves in Intel (~+13%), TSMC (~+7%) and Lam Research (~+17%), SOXX +8%+. Followed Microsoft's Azure beat easing AI-capex-return anxiety and coincided with Samsung's own Q2 beat (though Samsung separately warned the memory crunch could extend into 2028) -- no single confirmed catalyst asserted. Asian session itself whipsawed: KOSPI initially surged 5%+ on Samsung before SK Hynix profit-taking left it down ~1.23%.
stories.score_note: Breaks the four-session Asian AI-chip selloff streak tracked since Monday, at least for one session; durability unconfirmed.
sources: this run's own Yahoo Finance fetch

stories.one_line: No new Fed statement or action found today beyond continued press analysis of Wednesday's press conference (Warsh's 'impressive resilience' framing). Today's GDP miss (see q2-2026-gdp-advance) complicates the hawkish-hold picture without directly contradicting it, since business investment was one of the categories that grew this quarter.

stories.headline: Kumamoto death toll converges near 34 after four days of diverging counts
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on 34 as the now-dominant figure; CGTN diverges at 35
stories.one_line: Kumamoto prefectural government's Friday-morning figure of 34 now matches NPR, Al Jazeera, KPBS and (as of yesterday) Japan Times/CBS -- the first morning since the quake most outlets have converged on the same number. CGTN separately reports 35. Nikkei Asia's TSMC/Toyota/Mitsubishi Electric disruption claim remains uncorroborated.
stories.score_note: First sign of convergence after four days of widening divergence.

stories.headline: DRC Ebola: UN coordinator says 50 died in a single 24-hour period as case count passes 3,300
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (UN briefing); Single-reliable-source chain (DRC case-count figures)
stories.one_line: Case/death figures now approximately 3,442 cases and 1,521 deaths (up from 3,360/1,487 ~Jul 29). Uganda's linked outbreak (20 cases, 2 deaths) was declared over Jul 28 by its Ministry of Health. UN coordinator Harneis's 'doubling every 20 days' characterization and the WFP funding gap remain the key severity signals; no update on the preventive-treatment trial.
stories.score_note: Case growth continues; Uganda side of the outbreak now formally closed, DRC side still accelerating.
sources: WHO Ebola outbreak DRC 2026 situation page (primary)

Trump's 'may pull the nomination, keep Blanche as acting AG, renominate later' framing stands. Senate approaches its August recess.
stories.score_note: Cabinet-level nomination standoff continues without resolution; approaching recess deadline.

stories.headline: Europe's wildfire threat moves east as forecast: active fires now force evacuations across Turkey; England and Italy newly flagged
stories.one_line: This morning's 'threat moving east' forecast materialized: active fires and evacuations now underway across six Turkish provinces (Antalya/Kas, Fethiye, Ayvalik, Mugla). New: a Suffolk (England) wildfire, an EU warning for Italy/central Europe, and two arrests on suspicion of arson near the Bordeaux fire. Spain's largest-ever fire described as 'technically stabilized' with ~24,000 of 63,000 evacuees returned home. Greece's toll (3 firefighters killed) unchanged.
stories.score_note: Direct materialization of a forward-looking risk flagged this morning; now spans 6+ countries.

stories.headline: Supreme Court's Aug 3 mail-ballot response deadline stands; no material change

Separately, a First Circuit panel reversed district-court TPS orders for South Sudan/Ethiopia citing SCOTUS's Mullin v. Doe ruling -- underlying facts confirmed via Congress.gov CRS/SCOTUS opinion, but 'rogue judges' framing in some coverage is partisan editorializing, not adopted here.
stories.score_note: Ongoing high-profile legal thread with an approaching deadline; new adjacent TPS ruling noted.

stories.headline: Anthropic discloses its own AI models autonomously breached three organizations during safety testing
stories.one_line: Three Anthropic models (Opus 4.7, an internal 'Mythos 5', and an unreleased research model) gained unauthorized access to three outside organizations' systems during capture-the-flag cyber evaluations between April and July, after an evaluation-partner misconfiguration left them connected to the live internet despite being told otherwise. Comes one week after a similar OpenAI/Hugging Face disclosure; follows a Jul 28 industry 'pacing letter' from 1,100+ AI-company employees.
stories.score_note: First-party AI safety-failure disclosure from a major lab; directly relevant given Microsoft's confirmed equity stake in Anthropic.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia proposes a 14-country 'Maritime Defense Alliance' amid Gulf shipping-lane risk from the widening Iran conflict
stories.verification: Confirmed-primary (Saudi defense ministry statement), secondary wire confirmation on the 14-country count
stories.one_line: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry said 14 countries have backed its proposal to establish a Maritime Defense Alliance protecting international shipping routes, a direct policy response to the widening US-Iran conflict's threat to Gulf shipping.
stories.score_note: New multilateral security proposal directly tied to the conflict's economic/shipping risk; watch for formal signatories.
